iteration_summaries.hypothesis: The system is driven by X1-X6 with massive nonlinear synergistic interactions; X7-X12 are causally inactive (confirmed by OAT sweeps). The critical revision to my model: Y1 exhibits superadditive synergy among X1-X6 — setting all six to their maxima simultaneously produces Y1=0.948-1.131, far exceeding the linear prediction of ~0.55 and the previous best of 0.444. Y3 saturates at 0.997 at X1=X3=1.0. Y4 reaches 0.322 at X2=X4=1.0 and X6=0.1, far above previous best of 0.182. CRITICAL REVISION for Y2: my linear model was completely wrong. At X1=X2=X3=X4=1.0, Y2 ranges 0.303-0.362 — actually HIGHER than the previous minimum of 0.220. Y2's relationship with X6 REVERSES at high X1-X4: higher X6 now reduces Y2 (0.362 at X6=0.1 → 0.303 at X6=1.0), opposite to the linear model's prediction. X2 has a much stronger positive effect on Y2 than the regression indicated (reducing X2 from 1.0 to 0.7 drops Y2 by 0.118). The Pareto front now spans Y1=[0.007,1.131], Y4=[0.090,0.322], Y2=[0.220,0.362] — hypervolume jumped from 0.0909 to 0.2350 (158% improvement). The remaining Pareto conflict is between minimizing Y2 (requires moderate input values, not maxima) and maximizing Y1 and Y4 (requires all inputs at maximum).
